messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating‑point addition is performed with a finite number of bits, so after each operation the exact real sum is rounded to the nearest representable value. Because rounding is applied after every intermediate addition, the accumulated rounding error can differ depending on how the operands are grouped; for example, (a + b) + c may round a + b before adding c, while a + (b + c) rounds b + c first, leading to different final results. Consequently, the rounding step breaks the mathematical property (x + y) + z = x + (y + z), making floating‑point addition non‑associative.
